content.text: {"branch":"loan_originator","agent_name":"Loan Origination Researcher","status":"completed","summary":"For conventional conforming underwriting, substituting a rental AVM for proof of actual rental income would be a material policy change, not a simple documentation modernization. Current Fannie Mae policy uses market-rent evidence in bounded cases, but generally requires tax-return history or a fully executed lease plus corroboration of either market rent or actual payment performance. The operational upside is faster, more standardized first-pass assessment and less manual documentation; the central origination risk is that an AVM measures estimated market rent, not the borrower’s realized and continuing cash flow or lease authenticity. A prudent design would treat rental AVMs as a supplement, or restrict primary reliance to high-confidence, low-risk cases with conservative haircuts, validation, exception controls, and fair-lending/model-risk monitoring.","claims":[{"claim_id":"c1","text":"Current conforming guidance already permits market-rent evidence, but does not generally treat it as a universal substitute for proof of a borrower’s realized rental income. Fannie Mae requires tax returns for established non-subject rentals except documented exceptions; where leases or market rents are used, Form 1007/1025 or evidence that lease payments have begun is required.","claim_type":"fact","why_it_matters":"The proposed substitution would relax two distinct controls: evidence of the property’s market-rent potential and evidence that a tenant obligation is authentic and producing cash flow.","manager_implication":"Do not characterize rental-AVM substitution as aligning with the present conventional baseline. Specify the eligible transaction types and which existing corroboration requirements, if any, remain.","supporting_source_ids":["s_fannie_guide","s_fannie_quality"],"contradicting_source_ids":[],"evidence_strength":"strong","confidence":0.96,"geographic_scope":"United States; Fannie Mae conventional conforming loans","applicable_period":"Current guide published 2026-08-05; policy section dated 2025-10-08","material_limitations":["This establishes Fannie Mae requirements, not those of every portfolio, government, or non-QM lender.","The question does not specify whether the AVM would replace tenant receipts, leases, tax returns, appraiser market-rent schedules, or all such documentation."],"originating_agent":"loan_originator"},{"claim_id":"c2","text":"A rental AVM can plausibly improve origination speed, consistency, and capacity by automating a first-pass market-rent estimate, especially where a borrower has no rental history or a property is newly placed in service. However, this is an operational inference rather than evidence that approval quality or loan performance improves.","claim_type":"interpretation","why_it_matters":"Manual collection and review of leases, bank deposits, tax returns, and rent schedules consumes underwriting capacity and can delay decisions; an instant estimate can reduce that workflow burden.","manager_implication":"If explored, define AVM use as a workflow and triage tool first, and require a pilot to measure turn times, manual touches, override rates, and defect rates before expanding qualifying use.","supporting_source_ids":["s_fannie_guide","s_vendor_rental_avm"],"contradicting_source_ids":[],"evidence_strength":"moderate","confidence":0.76,"geographic_scope":"United States","applicable_period":"Current market and policy context","material_limitations":["The vendor source is a product claim, not independent performance evidence.","No validated study was located that estimates the effect of rental-AVM substitution on mortgage approval accuracy, default, or lender costs."],"originating_agent":"loan_originator"},{"claim_id":"c3","text":"Replacing receipt or payment evidence with a rental AVM risks overstating qualifying income when the property is vacant, leased below market, subject to concessions, restricted rents, tenant nonpayment, or borrower-specific management constraints. Fannie Mae’s current 75% calculation for market rent or lease rent explicitly reserves 25% for vacancy and ongoing maintenance, and it separately requires evidence that a lease has taken effect when relying on a lease.","claim_type":"synthesis","why_it_matters":"Estimated market rent and collected rent are different underwriting variables. If the estimate is treated as realized income, debt-to-income capacity may be overstated and pricing/risk segmentation weakened.","manager_implication":"Retain a conservative haircut at least calibrated to vacancy and expense experience; prohibit use above verified lease/receipt amounts when those are available; and use actual collection history for renewals, refinances, or existing rentals unless a narrowly documented exception applies.","supporting_source_ids":["s_fannie_guide","s_fannie_quality"],"contradicting_source_ids":[],"evidence_strength":"strong","confidence":0.92,"geographic_scope":"United States; Fannie Mae conventional conforming loans","applicable_period":"Current baseline","material_limitations":["The appropriate haircut for a rental-AVM policy cannot be inferred from Fannie Mae’s 25% convention alone; it requires portfolio- and geography-specific calibration.","This finding addresses underwriting mechanism, not borrower welfare or realized default outcomes."],"originating_agent":"loan_originator"},{"claim_id":"c4","text":"Substitution could weaken fraud and occupancy controls. Fannie Mae identifies falsified leases and primary-occupancy misrepresentation involving a departing residence as observed rental-income quality issues; removing receipt verification would eliminate one independent check that a represented tenancy is producing payments.","claim_type":"fact","why_it_matters":"Originators have incentives to close borderline loans, while secondary-market and insurer exposure often emerges later. Less borrower-specific evidence increases the importance of independent controls and post-close review.","manager_implication":"Require occupancy-risk flags, fraud-screening rules, deposit/first-payment verification for new leases, and enhanced review for departing-residence and investor scenarios. The rule’s controls—confidence, anti-manipulation, conflict management, random testing, and nondiscrimination compliance—are relevant risk-control analogies, not direct proof that the rule governs rental AVMs.","claim_type":"interpretation","why_it_matters":"Rent-estimation inputs and performance may vary by geography, property type, data coverage, and protected-class-correlated neighborhood characteristics. An originator remains responsible for underwriting outcomes and vendor oversight even when a third party supplies the model.","manager_implication":"Treat a rental AVM as a material underwriting model/vendor: document intended use, validation population, error and confidence thresholds, geographic/property exclusions, overrides, adverse-action reason mapping where relevant, audit trails, and periodic disparate-outcome testing.","supporting_source_ids":["s_cfpb_avm_rule","s_cfpb_avm_preamble"],"contradicting_source_ids":[],"evidence_strength":"moderate","confidence":0.85,"geographic_scope":"United States","applicable_period":"Interagency final rule issued 2024; implementation context current as of 2026-08-19","material_limitations":["The cited rule covers collateral-value AVMs; applying its control concepts to rental AVMs is an analytical recommendation, not a legal conclusion.","No consensus standard for rental-AVM accuracy, confidence reporting, or fairness testing was identified."],"originating_agent":"loan_originator"},{"claim_id":"c6","text":"The policy can create adverse selection and competition effects: lenders that credit high rental-AVM estimates most aggressively may attract borrowers and properties for which estimated market rent is least predictive of realized collections. This risk should be expected to concentrate in thin-data areas, atypical properties, and rapidly changing rental markets unless eligibility and pricing respond to confidence and error.","claim_type":"forecast","why_it_matters":"Competition on the most permissive estimate can shift risk into originators, investors, guarantors, or insurers, while an undifferentiated rule may disadvantage lenders that maintain stronger verification controls.","manager_implication":"Use confidence-based eligibility rather than universal substitution; compare AVM estimates against later leases and collections by geography, property type, borrower/risk tier, and channel; and price or decline cases outside validated model bounds.","supporting_source_ids":["s_fannie_guide","s_cfpb_avm_preamble","s_vendor_rental_avm"],"contradicting_source_ids":[],"evidence_strength":"moderate","confidence":0.71,"geographic_scope":"United States","applicable_period":"5-to-10-year policy horizon","material_limitations":["This is a mechanism-based forecast, not a causal estimate from a rental-AVM mortgage pilot.","The magnitude depends on investor acceptance, capital treatment, fraud controls, rental-market volatility, and model coverage."],"originating_agent":"loan_originator"},{"claim_id":"c7","text":"The evidence supports a differentiated product design rather than one rule for all workflows. Market-rent estimates are most conceptually suitable for prospective rent on a newly acquired or newly converted property; they are less suitable for replacing historic cash-flow documentation on an established rental, where tax returns and payment records provide borrower- and property-specific performance information.","claim_type":"synthesis","why_it_matters":"The incremental information supplied by an AVM is greatest where no operating history exists, while the information lost by dropping actual evidence is greatest where an operating history is available.","manager_implication":"If piloted, limit AVM-primary use to prospective-rent cases;
